rows.fidelity_note: The formal assertion concerns a real Hilbert space with the stipulated heat, dilation and bilinear operators and a nonzero continuous recurrent mild profile $w(s+S)=\rho w(s)$, $S>0$. For a subdivision into $k\ge1$ pieces on which each linearized Duhamel operator has norm at most $1/4$, it states that the period operator $M$ differs compactly from its free heat-and-dilation counterpart $M_0$, and $\|M_0\|\le e^{-S/4}<1$. rows.name: Breakdown.MonodromyStatement
rows.plain: Short-step inverses and the compact monodromy correction
rows.annotation: In the period map the initial datum is varied, while the reference $u^*(t')$ in the mixed integral is fixed at each $t'$. Lemma 3.2 gives norm-null integrands for weakly null linearized trajectories, and (3.7) gives an integrable majorant. For the formal short-step proof, fix a test factor $f$ and truncate the last $\epsilon$ units, at cost $O(\epsilon^{1/4})$. At the remaining lags use $K(\tau)(f,\cdot)=G(\tau-\epsilon)K(\epsilon)(f,\cdot)$: the heat images of the compact closure at lag $\epsilon$ have compact closure over the bounded time interval. Approximation of the continuous coefficient curve by finite sums of such factors gives compactness of the mixed endpoint integral. The full return is obtained by composing short steps.

merged.quote:
**Lemma 3.3.** Let $a\le b$, and let $u,v:[a,b]\to\mathcal X$ be continuous. Then for every $t\in[a,b]$ the map $t'\mapsto K(t-t')(u(t'),v(t'))$ is integrable on $[a,t]$, and the map $$
t\mapsto\int_a^t K(t-t')(u(t'),v(t'))\,dt'
$$ is continuous on $[a,b]$.

ties.name: Breakdown.VarConstIntegralStatement
ties.plain: Continuity of the Duhamel integral

assessments.fidelity_note: Let $\mathcal X$ be a real Banach space, $G(t)$ a strongly continuous contraction semigroup for $t\ge0$, and $K(\tau)$ symmetric bounded bilinear maps, continuous for each fixed pair of arguments when $\tau>0$. Assume $G(s)K(\tau)(u,v)=K(s+\tau)(u,v)$ for $s\ge0,\tau>0$ and $\|K(\tau)\|\le C_K\tau^{-3/4}$ for $0<\tau\le1$. If $a\le b$ and $u,v$ are continuous on $[a,b]$, with $\|u(s)\|\le M$ and $\|v(s)\|\le N$ throughout, then $I(t)=\int_a^tK(t-s)(u(s),v(s))\,ds$ is Bochner integrable for every $t\in[a,b]$ and continuous in $t$. When $t-a\le1$, $\|I(t)\|\le4C_K(t-a)^{1/4}MN$. Such $M,N$ exist by compactness. This includes Lemma 3.3 and an additional short-time estimate under a weaker lag-bound hypothesis. This linked definition states the assertion.

rows.name: Breakdown.varConstIntegral
rows.plain: Continuity and bounds for Duhamel terms
rows.annotation: Put $T=b-a$ and change variables to $\tau=t-t\prime$. Extend the inputs by their endpoint values and integrate $K(\tau)(u(t-\tau),v(t-\tau))$ over $(0,T)$ with the indicator of $\tau<t-a$. For a fixed positive $\tau\ne t-a$ the integrand is continuous in $t$. Its norm has a common integrable majorant, $C_KMN\tau^{-3/4}$ up to lag one and $C_KMN$ thereafter in Lean. Dominated convergence proves continuity also at $a,b$.

ties.name: Breakdown.PieceOperatorStatement
ties.plain: Uniform bounds for the Duhamel operator on a compact time interval

rows.fidelity_note: Let $\mathcal X$ be a real Banach space, $G(t)$ a strongly continuous contraction semigroup for $t\ge0$, and $K(\tau)$ symmetric bounded bilinear maps, continuous for each fixed pair of arguments when $\tau>0$. Assume $G(s)K(\tau)(u,v)=K(s+\tau)(u,v)$ for $s\ge0,\tau>0$ and $\|K(\tau)\|\le C_K\tau^{-3/4}$ for $0<\tau\le1$. For $T>0$, the formal assertion identifies $B_T:C([0,T];\mathcal X)^2\to C([0,T];\mathcal X)$ by $B_T(f,h)(t)=\int_0^tK(t-s)(f(s),h(s))\,ds$ and proves bounded bilinearity; $\|B_T\|\le4C_KT^{1/4}$ when $T\le1$. It also identifies $\Gamma_T:\mathcal X\to C([0,T];\mathcal X)$ by $\Gamma_Tx(t)=G(t)x$, with norm at most one. Translating time gives the integral operator in Lemma 3.4; invertibility of $I-2B_T(f,\cdot)$ on an arbitrary interval is a further conclusion. The linked definition states these operator properties.
rows.name: Breakdown.PieceOperatorStatement
rows.plain: Uniform bounds for the Duhamel operator on a compact time interval
rows.annotation: The mixed term in the expansion at $f$ of $K(\tau)(f+h,f+h)$ is $2K(\tau)(f,h)$. Its time integral is linear in $h$ and its size need not be small. The source $g$ may be any continuous curve: setting $t=a$ gives $h(a)=g(a)$. `PieceOperatorStatement` supplies the bounded time-integral map and the free-heat map on a short interval.

rows.name: Breakdown.pieceOperator
rows.plain: Bounded Duhamel and heat maps on one time interval
rows.annotation: On an interval of length $T\le1$ the operator $Ah=2\int_a^t K(t-t')(f(t'),h(t'))dt'$ has norm at most $8C_KT^{1/4}\|f\|_C$. Thus any bounded $f$ can be treated on sufficiently short intervals. This is the local bound used in Lean to invert $I-A$; Appendix A.1 instead changes the norm on the entire interval.

rows.fidelity_note: For a bounded operator $A$ on a real Banach space with $\|A\|<1$, the formal theorem gives $h-Ah=g$ for $h=(I-A)^{-1}g$ and every $g$. Taking $A h(t)=2\int_a^tK(t-s)(f(s),h(s))\,ds$ requires a separate smallness estimate in this norm. Lemma 3.4 asserts invertibility of this Volterra equation for every continuous $f$ and every finite interval, without that norm-smallness assumption.
rows.name: Breakdown.Periodic.InverseAlgebra.Internal.sub_apply_inverse_one_sub
rows.plain: The Neumann inverse solves the perturbed identity equation
rows.annotation: The paper makes $A:h\mapsto2\int_a^t K(t-t')(f(t'),h(t'))dt'$ small without changing the length of the interval. The exponential weight in Appendix A.1 gives $\|A\|_\beta\le2C_K\|f\|_C\int_0^\infty e^{-\beta\tau}\tau^{-3/4}d\tau=2C_K\|f\|_C\Gamma(1/4)\beta^{-1/4}$. For sufficiently large $\beta$, $h=(I-A)^{-1}g$. The linked identity is the algebraic verification of this solution once $I-A$ has been proved invertible.

ties.name: Breakdown.Periodic.InverseAlgebra.Internal.norm_inverse_one_sub_le
ties.plain: Neumann inverse bound for perturbation norm ≤ q < 1

rows.fidelity_note: For a bounded operator $A$ on a real Banach space and $\|A\|\le q<1$, the formal theorem proves $\|(I-A)^{-1}\|\le(1-q)^{-1}$. The paper’s sentence concerns the solution operator of $h(t)=2\int_a^tK(t-s)(f(s),h(s))\,ds+g(t)$ on any finite $[a,b]$. It imposes no smallness of the Volterra operator in the supremum norm; the linked inverse estimate requires that additional hypothesis.
rows.name: Breakdown.Periodic.InverseAlgebra.Internal.norm_inverse_one_sub_le
rows.plain: Neumann inverse bound for perturbation norm ≤ q < 1
rows.annotation: For the weighted norm choose $q<1$ bounding the norm of the linear integral operator. The geometric series gives $\|(I-A)^{-1}\|_\beta\le(1-q)^{-1}$. Since $\|h\|_\beta\le\|h\|_\infty\le e^{\beta(b-a)}\|h\|_\beta$, the unweighted bound is $\|h\|_\infty\le e^{\beta(b-a)}(1-q)^{-1}\|g\|_\infty$. This is a bound for a fixed finite interval and fixed $f$, not a uniform bound over all $f$ or interval lengths.

rows.fidelity_note: Let $\mathcal X$ be a real Banach space, $G(t)$ a strongly continuous contraction semigroup for $t\ge0$, and $K(\tau)$ symmetric bounded bilinear maps, continuous for each fixed pair of arguments when $\tau>0$. Assume $G(s)K(\tau)(u,v)=K(s+\tau)(u,v)$ for $s\ge0,\tau>0$ and $\|K(\tau)\|\le C_K\tau^{-3/4}$ for $0<\tau\le1$. Let $a\le m\le t$ and let $u$ be continuous on $[a,t]$. rows.annotation: Lean proves the identity by a backward heat test. Test the weak equation first with $-\Delta\psi$ to obtain an equation in the gradient pairing of $X$, then extend it by graph-norm density to heat-smoothed tests. For a fixed terminal time $t$ and $\varepsilon>0$, use $e^{(t-s+\varepsilon)\Delta}\psi$ at time $s$. Differentiation in $s$ produces $-\Delta$ on this test, cancelling the diffusion in the weak equation. The derivative of the pairing is then $\langle K(t-s+\varepsilon)(u(s),u(s)),\psi\rangle_X$. Integrate over $[a,t]$. The positive terminal lag permits all the test derivatives even at $s=t$. This proof uses the additional hypotheses of `IsWeakSolution`.

rows.plain: The periodic bilinear kernel satisfies the τ⁻³⁄⁴ bound
rows.annotation: Lean first estimates $K(\tau)(u,u)$ by pairing its weighted Fourier coefficients with the heat-smoothed advection. The trilinear bound gives a diagonal estimate $\|K(\tau)(u,u)\|\le D_\tau\|u\|^2$ with $D_\tau=O(\tau^{-3/4})$. rows.annotation: For a physical interval beginning at $t_0$ and of length $\mu(1-\lambda)$ set $U(s)=\mu^{1/4}u(t_0+\mu s)$. rows.annotation: The operator $D_\mu$ in (3.21) changes the spatial period to $L/\sqrt\mu$. `stepFrame` does not perform that spatial dilation. rows.name: Breakdown.orbitNorm
rows.plain: A recurrent mild orbit has a uniform positive norm lower bound
rows.annotation: The formal lower bound uses a small-data estimate rather than the first-period minimum. If $\|W(s_0)\|_X\le c_{\rm small}$, the physical mild solution starting there satisfies $\|u(t)\|_X\le2\|W(s_0)\|_X$ up to time one. ties.name: Breakdown.physicalTime
ties.plain: Logarithmic similarity time at final time one

rows.name: Breakdown.physicalTime
rows.plain: Logarithmic similarity time at final time one
rows.annotation: The map $t\mapsto1-\lambda(1-t)$ reduces the remaining time by $\lambda$; indeed $-\log(\lambda(1-t))=-\log(1-t)+S$. It is a translation in similarity time. This makes the linear evolution on different physical periods comparable after rescaling.

ties.name: Breakdown.MildFramework.gluePieces
ties.plain: Joining rescaled time intervals

rows.fidelity_note: For $0<\mu<1$ and continuous curves $a_n:[0,1-\mu]\to X$ in a real Hilbert space with dilations $D_\mu$, the formal reconstruction is $v(t)=D_{\mu^{-n}}a_n(\sigma)$, $n=\lfloor\log(1-t)/\log\mu\rfloor_{\mathbb N}$ and $\sigma=(t-(1-\mu^n))/\mu^n$. On $0\le t<1$ this gives $0\le\sigma<1-\mu$ and $1-t=\mu^n(1-\sigma)$. The natural-number floor is zero on negative inputs. Outside each interval a curve is extended by its endpoint value. The formal construction generally takes $\mu=e^{-S/k}$, so one similarity period contains $k$ short intervals. The paper's times $t_n=1-\lambda^n$, $\lambda=e^{-S}$, are whole-period endpoints. They correspond to $k=1$, or to every kth short endpoint. Neither recurrence nor a norm rate is a conclusion of the reconstruction definition.
rows.name: Breakdown.MildFramework.gluePieces
rows.plain: Joining rescaled time intervals
rows.annotation: In the formal gluing take $\mu=e^{-S/k}$, $t_j=1-\mu^j$ and $\sigma=(t-t_j)/\mu^j$. The physical field on that piece is $D_{\mu^{-j}}u_j(\sigma)$. The matching condition $u_{j+1}(0)=D_\mu u_j(1-\mu)$ makes the two formulas agree at $t_{j+1}$, since $D_{\mu^{-(j+1)}}D_\mu=D_{\mu^{-j}}$. Thus solutions on the same normalized interval join continuously at the physical endpoints.

rows.name: Breakdown.stepData
rows.plain: A bounded right inverse for the linearized interval equations
rows.annotation: For the short pieces set $\mu=e^{-S/k}$ and choose $\mu^{1/4}<\theta<1$. Write the normalized perturbation on piece $j$ as $\theta^j z_j$. A decay bound becomes a supremum bound on $z_j$, and matching requires the next weighted datum to be $\theta^{-1}D_\mu z_j(1-\mu)$. `stepData` solves the linear recursion with these factors and a freely chosen finite-dimensional correction on the first piece. The resulting decay rate is $-\log\theta/(S/k)$, between zero and $1/4$.

assessments.fidelity_note: Let $X$ be a real Banach space, $P:X\to X$ a bounded projection with finite-dimensional range, and $C\subset X$ a dense linear subspace. The theorem gives a bounded linear $J:X\to X$ with $PJ=P$ and $J(X)\subset C$. The restriction of $J$ to $\operatorname{ran}P$ is injective, so $E=J(\operatorname{ran}P)$ is finite-dimensional. Taking $C=C^\infty_{c,\mathrm{div}}$ inside $\dot H^1_{\mathrm{div}}$ supplies the correction space in the paper. The theorem supplies no inverse for the evolution equation or global weighted curve.

rows.name: Breakdown.exists_section
rows.plain: Lifting a finite-dimensional projection
rows.annotation: The exterior projection $P_u$ will have finite-dimensional range $V$. The image $P_u C'$ of the dense test subspace is dense in $V$ and, being a linear subspace of $V$, is closed; hence it equals $V$. Lift a basis of $V$ to test fields. The restriction of $P_u$ to their span is an isomorphism onto $V$; its inverse gives the compactly supported lift, extended to a bounded map $J$ with $P_uJ=P_u$. The lift may have a stable component; no compact support of spectral vectors is required.

rows.name: Breakdown.orbitNorm
rows.plain: A recurrent mild orbit has a uniform positive norm lower bound
rows.annotation: Once the first-period norm has positive minimum, the scaling formula propagates it to all subsequent periods. `orbitNorm` gets positivity by another route: a similarity slice below the small-data threshold would have a physical evolution bounded through time one, incompatible with recurrence. The lower bound is used later in the reverse triangle inequality for the corrected flow.

assessments.fidelity_note: In $X=\dot H^1_{\mathrm{div}}(\mathbb R^3)$, with norm $\|u\|_X=\|\nabla u\|_2$, the formal assertion requires, for $\mu,\eta>0$, $\|D_\mu x\|_X=\mu^{1/4}\|x\|_X$, $D_1=I$, $D_\mu D_\eta=D_{\mu\eta}$ and $D_\mu G(\mu t)=G(t)D_\mu$ for $t\ge0$. rows.plain: Dilation of solenoidal fields
rows.annotation: In (4.3) the isometry has norm one, and $D_{\lambda^{-n}}$ multiplies the gradient norm by $\lambda^{-n/4}$. Therefore $(1-t)^{1/4}\|u^*(t)\|_X=(1-\sigma)^{1/4}\|u^*(\sigma)\|_X$. rows.name: Breakdown.monodromy
rows.plain: Monodromy is a compact perturbation of free evolution
rows.annotation: The dilation in (4.3) is undone when defining the return of a linearized perturbation. If $h_\chi$ solves (4.9), then $M\chi=\rho_R^{-1}D_\lambda h_\chi(t_1)$. rows.name: Breakdown.MonodromyStatement
rows.plain: Short-step inverses and the compact monodromy correction
rows.annotation: For a subdivision into $k$ short intervals, $\mu=e^{-S/k}$. The linearized integral operator $A_j$ has norm at most $1/4$, so $(I-A_j)^{-1}$ has norm at most $4/3$. The short return $L_j$ evolves with this inverse and restores scale by $D_\mu$. The full return is $\rho_R^{-1}L_{k-1}\cdots L_0$. Each free short return has norm at most $\mu^{1/4}$, hence the product has norm at most $e^{-S/4}$. Compactness of the difference survives the finite composition: the difference of products is a finite sum with at least one compact factor in each summand.

assessments.fidelity_note: Let $X$ be a real Hilbert space and $M=T_0+C$, where $T_0,C$ are bounded linear operators, $C$ is compact and $\|T_0\|\le b\le\alpha<\beta$ with $b\ge0$. assessments.fidelity_note: Let $X$ be a real Banach space, $G(t)$ a strongly continuous contraction semigroup for $t\ge0$, and $K(\tau):X\times X\to X$ symmetric bounded bilinear maps. assessments.fidelity_note: Let $X,Y$ be real Banach spaces, $k\ge1$, $\theta>0$, and let $\rho:X\to X$ be a surjective linear isometry. Set $S_n=E(I-A_n)^{-1}\Gamma$ and $M=\rho^{-1}S_{k-1}\cdots S_0$, and assume $S_{n+k}=\rho S_n\rho^{-1}$, $P^2=P$, $PM=MP$, $PJ=P$. For $0\le r_1<\theta^k<r_2$, require $\|M^n(I-P)\|\le Kr_1^n$, $\|Px\|\le Kr_2^{-n}\|M^nPx\|$ for all $n\ge0,x\in X$, and surjectivity of $M$ on $\operatorname{ran}P$. For $(e,z)=\mathcal Rg$, it requires $e\in\operatorname{ran}P$, $z_0-A_0z_0-\Gamma Je=g_0$ and $z_n-A_nz_n-\theta^{-1}\Gamma Ez_{n-1}=g_n$ for $n\ge1$. rows.annotation: On one divided piece, let $x_n$ denote the incoming heat datum and put $U_n=(I-A_n)^{-1}$. The local solution is $U_n(\Gamma x_n+g_n)$. assessments.fidelity_note: Let $X$ be a real Hilbert space. Suppose $G(t)$, $t\ge0$, is a strongly continuous contraction semigroup and $K(\tau)$ is a symmetric bounded bilinear family, continuous on each pair of arguments for $\tau>0$, with $G(s)K(\tau)=K(s+\tau)$ and $\|K(\tau)\|\le C_K\tau^{-3/4}$ for $0<\tau\le1$. For $\mu>0$, suppose the dilations are strongly continuous, $D_1=I$, $D_\mu D_\eta=D_{\mu\eta}$, $\|D_\mu x\|=\mu^{1/4}\|x\|$, $D_\mu G(\mu t)=G(t)D_\mu$ for $t\ge0$, and $\mu D_\mu K(\mu\tau)(x,y)=K(\tau)(D_\mu x,D_\mu y)$ for $\tau>0$. For a dense set of $f\in X$, require $K(\tau)(f,\cdot)$ compact for every $\tau>0$. Let $\rho$ be a surjective linear isometry commuting with $G,K,D$, including their assigned values at all real parameters. Let $S>0$ and let $w:\mathbb R\to X$ be continuous and nonzero somewhere, with $w(s+S)=\rho w(s)$. For $a\le s$, require the Bochner integral to exist and $w(s)=D_{e^{-(s-a)}}G(1-e^{-(s-a)})w(a)+\int_a^sD_{e^{-(s-r)}}K(1-e^{-(s-r)})(w(r),w(r))\,dr$. rows.annotation: Choose the subdivision before the spectral radius. With $\mu=e^{-S/k}$ and $M=\sup_s\|W(s)\|_X$, the mixed operator on each piece has norm at most $8C_K M(e^{S/k}-1)^{1/4}$. ties.name: Breakdown.PieceOperatorStatement
ties.plain: Uniform bounds for the Duhamel operator on a compact time interval

rows.fidelity_note: Let $X$ be a real Banach space, $G(t)$ a strongly continuous contraction semigroup for $t\ge0$, and $K(\tau):X\times X\to X$ symmetric bounded bilinear maps. rows.plain: Uniform bounds for the Duhamel operator on a compact time interval
rows.annotation: In (4.8), $e^{t\Delta}\gamma$ means the entire heat curve. ties.name: Breakdown.orbitSeq
ties.plain: Weighted monodromy recurrence with forcing

rows.fidelity_note: For a bounded linear operator $M$ on a real normed space, a real $\theta$, a prescribed source sequence $c_n$ and an initial value $x_0$, the formal definition is $x_{n+1}=\theta^{-1}(Mx_n+c_n)$ for natural $n$. It has no boundedness or decay conclusion. At $\theta=0$ division is assigned zero; the dichotomy arguments impose $\theta>0$. If the unweighted recurrence is $\chi_{n+1}=M\chi_n+f_n$, then $x_n=\theta^{-n}\chi_n$ and $c_n=\theta^{-n}f_n$ give the formal formula for $\theta>0$. The paper's decay relative to $u^*$ also uses the physical dilation factor; the recurrence definition supplies no estimate for that curve.
rows.name: Breakdown.orbitSeq
rows.plain: Weighted monodromy recurrence with forcing
rows.annotation: For $v\in C_\kappa$, the norm of its endpoint after returning to the first period is at most $\Theta^n\|v\|_\kappa$. Since $g$ belongs to the same space, subtracting its normalized endpoint changes the bound to $\Theta^n(\|v\|_\kappa+\|g\|_\kappa)$. Thus one may impose the same decay on the propagated variable $v-g$.

rows.fidelity_note: For any curve $w:\mathbb R\to X$ in a real Hilbert space with dilation maps $D_\mu$, the formal function is $u_{s_0}(t)=D_{(1-t)^{-1}}w(s_0-\log(1-t))$. On $t<1$ its scale is positive; the definition requires no recurrence, continuity or equation. In the physical realization $D_\mu f(x)=\sqrt\mu f(\sqrt\mu x)$. For $s=-\log(1-t)$, $(1-t)^{-\kappa}=e^{\kappa s}$ on $t<1$. The paper combines this identity with the dilation norm law and a positive profile lower bound to compare $v$ with $u^*$. The formal definition states the change of variables only and includes no weighted norm or bound.
rows.name: Breakdown.MildFramework.selfSimilar
rows.plain: An orbit in physical time
rows.annotation: `selfSimilar` uses a phase $s_0$ and local time $t$: the physical field is $D_{(1-t)^{-1}}w(s_0-\log(1-t))$. Applying the gradient scaling gives $(1-t)^{-1/4}$ times the profile norm. The norm (4.5) consequently measures the rescaled error with the additional factor $e^{\kappa s}$.

ties.name: Breakdown.PiecePerturbationStatement
ties.plain: Mild equation for an approximate flow plus a correction

rows.name: Breakdown.PiecePerturbationStatement
rows.plain: Mild equation for an approximate flow plus a correction
rows.annotation: The error equation retains the two mixed terms as $2\mathcal B(u^*,v)$ and the entire quadratic term as $\mathcal B(v,v)$. Since $u^*$ is an exact solution, its pure term cancels. rows.name: Breakdown.stepData
rows.plain: A bounded right inverse for the linearized interval equations
rows.annotation: `stepData` constructs a right inverse on bounded sequences of divided pieces. It first makes each local linear equation invertible by choosing $k$, then uses the spectral splitting of the $k$-step return to choose the initial coefficient in a finite-dimensional range. This avoids trying to invert the mixed operator on the entire half-open interval by a Neumann series.

rows.fidelity_note: Let $X$ be a real Banach space, $P:X\to X$ a bounded projection with finite-dimensional range, and $C\subset X$ a dense linear subspace. The theorem gives a bounded linear $J:X\to X$ with $PJ=P$ and $J(X)\subset C$. The restriction of $J$ to $\operatorname{ran}P$ is injective, so $E=J(\operatorname{ran}P)$ is finite-dimensional. Taking $C=C^\infty_{c,\mathrm{div}}$ inside $\dot H^1_{\mathrm{div}}$ supplies the correction space in the paper. The theorem supplies no inverse for the evolution equation or global weighted curve.
rows.name: Breakdown.exists_section

rows.annotation: For a fixed $g$, any two admissible data in (4.12) differ by an element of $\ker P_{\mathrm u}$: their difference evolves homogeneously, and the inverse power bound forces its exterior projection to vanish. Conversely an interior displacement has the required decay. Taking the datum in the complementary space $E$ selects exactly one point of this affine space.

assessments.fidelity_note: For a sequence of operators $S_0,S_1,\ldots$, the formal definition is the ordered product $S_{k-1}\cdots S_0$, with $S_0$ acting first and the empty product equal to $I$ at $k=0$. It is defined for any monoid and contains no twist or evolution hypothesis. In the formal period construction the monodromy is $\rho_R^{-1}S_{k-1}\cdots S_0$; the extra factor and the identification of $S_n$ with linearized endpoint maps are separate from this definition.

rows.annotation: Let $M_j$ be the short endpoint maps and $Q=M_{k-1}\cdots M_0$. On the next block the product is $\rho_R Q\rho_R^{-1}$, since all intermediate conjugations cancel. In coordinates rotated back by $\rho_R^{-n}$ at block $n$, the homogeneous block update is always $\rho_R^{-1}Q$. This is the formal period map.

assessments.fidelity_note: Let $X$ be a real Hilbert space. Suppose $G(t)$, $t\ge0$, is a strongly continuous contraction semigroup and $K(\tau)$ is a symmetric bounded bilinear family, continuous on each pair of arguments for $\tau>0$, with $G(s)K(\tau)=K(s+\tau)$ and $\|K(\tau)\|\le C_K\tau^{-3/4}$ for $0<\tau\le1$. For $\mu>0$, suppose the dilations are strongly continuous, $D_1=I$, $D_\mu D_\eta=D_{\mu\eta}$, $\|D_\mu x\|=\mu^{1/4}\|x\|$, $D_\mu G(\mu t)=G(t)D_\mu$ for $t\ge0$, and $\mu D_\mu K(\mu\tau)(x,y)=K(\tau)(D_\mu x,D_\mu y)$ for $\tau>0$. For a dense set of $f\in X$, require $K(\tau)(f,\cdot)$ compact for every $\tau>0$. Let $\rho$ be a surjective linear isometry commuting with $G,K,D$, including their assigned values at all real parameters. Let $S>0$ and let $w:\mathbb R\to X$ be continuous and nonzero somewhere, with $w(s+S)=\rho w(s)$. For $a\le s$, require the Bochner integral to exist and $w(s)=D_{e^{-(s-a)}}G(1-e^{-(s-a)})w(a)+\int_a^sD_{e^{-(s-r)}}K(1-e^{-(s-r)})(w(r),w(r))\,dr$. Fix an integer $k\ge1$, put $\mu=e^{-S/k}$, $L=1-\mu$ and $a_n(t)=D_{(1-t)^{-1}}w(nS/k-\log(1-t))$ on $[0,L]$. On $Y=C([0,L];X)$ define $A_nz(t)=2\int_0^tK(t-r)(a_n(r),z(r))\,dr$, $\Gamma x(t)=G(t)x$ and $Ev=D_\mu v(L)$. The formal assertion assumes $\|A_n\|\le1/4$ for every $n$, and states that $I-A_n$ is invertible with inverse norm at most $4/3$. With $S_n=E(I-A_n)^{-1}\Gamma$, $\mathcal M=\rho^{-1}S_{k-1}\cdots S_0$ and $\mathcal M_0=\rho^{-1}(D_\mu G(L))^k$, it states $S_{n+k}=\rho S_n\rho^{-1}$, compactness of $\mathcal M-\mathcal M_0$, and $\|\mathcal M_0\|\le e^{-S/4}$. The paper defines $\mathcal M\chi=\rho_R^{-1}D_{e^{-S}}h_\chi(1-e^{-S})$ using a whole-period trajectory. The formal assertion uses the product of short-interval endpoint maps. Identifying those maps with the rescaled pieces of $h_\chi$ requires the evolution and matching argument; this identity with $h_\chi$ is not a stated conclusion. The comparison therefore records different formulations.

rows.name: Breakdown.MonodromyStatement
rows.plain: Short-step inverses and the compact monodromy correction
rows.annotation: The recurrence of the background multiplies it by $\rho_R D_{1/\lambda}$ over one period. Both operations are invertible and commute, so undoing them on the final perturbation gives exactly $\rho_R^{-1}D_\lambda h_\chi(t_1)$. This is why there is no forward rotation in (4.10).

ties.name: Breakdown.stepMap
ties.plain: One-step linearized evolution from the interval inverse

rows.fidelity_note: For real normed spaces $X,Y$ and bounded linear maps $A_n:Y\to Y$, $\Gamma:X\to Y$, $E:Y\to X$, the formal definition is $S_n=E(I-A_n)^{-1}\Gamma$. An operator without a bounded inverse is assigned inverse zero. If $I-A_n$ is invertible, $(I-A_n)^{-1}\Gamma x$ solves the linear interval equation, and $S_nx$ is its rescaled endpoint. In the application $Y=C([0,L];X)$, $\Gamma x(t)=G(t)x$, and $Ev=D_\mu v(L)$. Each formal $S_n$ is bounded and linear, including when the assigned inverse is zero. To obtain the paper's period map one needs genuine short-interval inverses, the finite product over a period, and the inverse isometry $\rho_R^{-1}$. This definition alone does not identify its output with a whole-period linearized flow.
rows.name: Breakdown.stepMap
rows.plain: One-step linearized evolution from the interval inverse
rows.annotation: The bound $(4/3)\mu^{1/4}$ on a short endpoint map need not be below one. In fact $\mu^{1/4}\to1$ as the pieces are shortened. The smallness estimate gives a bounded solution operator on each piece; decay over an entire period must come from the free comparison and the subsequent spectral argument.

rows.annotation: Write $Q_m=M_{m-1}\cdots M_0$ for the product of the actual short returns and $B$ for the free step. Then $Q_{m+1}-B^{m+1}=(M_m-B)Q_m+B(Q_m-B^m)$. Compact operators form a two-sided ideal, so compactness of each $M_m-B$ suffices by induction; one does not need compactness of $Q_m$ or of the free heat operator.

rows.plain: Short-step inverses and the compact monodromy correction
rows.annotation: A free step is $B=D_\mu e^{(1-\mu)\Delta}$, with norm at most $\mu^{1/4}$. The Lean proof only needs $\|B^k\|\le\mu^{k/4}$. To identify it with the paper’s free map, use (3.5): $B^2=D_{\mu^2}e^{(1-\mu^2)\Delta}$, since the heat times add as $(1-\mu)+\mu(1-\mu)$. Hence $B^k=D_\lambda e^{t_1\Delta}$ and $\rho_R^{-1}B^k$ is the desired return.

ties.name: Breakdown.Freq.DilationAlgebra
ties.plain: Dilation of solenoidal fields

rows.fidelity_note: The formal space $X$ is a frequency-side model of $\dot H^1_{\mathrm{div}}(\mathbb R^3)$: a closed subspace of $L^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C^3)$ of transverse fields with the reality symmetry, on which $G(t)$ is the multiplier $e^{-4\pi^2t|\xi|^2}$ and $D_\mu$ acts by $f(\xi)\mapsto\mu^{-1/2}f(\xi/\sqrt\mu)$, the frequency form of $D_\mu u(x)=\sqrt\mu\,u(\sqrt\mu x)$. For $\mu,\eta>0$ the formal assertion states $\|D_\mu x\|=\mu^{1/4}\|x\|$, $D_1=I$, $D_\mu D_\eta=D_{\mu\eta}$, $D_\mu G(\mu t)=G(t)D_\mu$ for $t\ge0$, and agreement of $D_\mu$ with the dilation on $L^2$. Taking $\mu=\lambda=e^{-S}$ gives the dilation factor $e^{-S/4}$. The paper's bound also uses $\|G(1-\lambda)\|\le1$ and the fact that $\rho_R^{-1}$ is an isometry. Neither heat contractivity nor the rotation norm is a conclusion of the dilation assertion itself.
rows.name: Breakdown.Freq.DilationAlgebra
rows.plain: Dilation of solenoidal fields
rows.annotation: The free comparison uses the exact same change of coordinates as the true return. Its three factors give $\|\rho_R^{-1}D_\lambda e^{t_1\Delta}x\|_X=\lambda^{1/4}\|e^{t_1\Delta}x\|_X\le\lambda^{1/4}\|x\|_X$. Neither the amplitude of $u^*$ nor its spectrum enters this bound.

ties.name: Breakdown.dichotomyHolds
ties.plain: Finite-dimensional monodromy splitting with separated power bounds

rows.fidelity_note: Let $X$ be a real Hilbert space and $M=T_0+C$, where $T_0,C$ are bounded linear operators, $C$ is compact and $\|T_0\|\le b\le\alpha<\beta$ with $b\ge0$. The formal assertion supplies $\alpha<r_1<r_2<\beta$, $K>0$ and a bounded finite-rank projection $P$ such that $PM=MP$, $\|M^n(I-P)\|\le Kr_1^n$ and $\|Px\|\le Kr_2^{-n}\|M^nPx\|$ for all natural $n$ and $x\in X$; $M$ maps $\operatorname{ran}P$ onto itself. The last two properties make the restricted operator $M_{\mathrm u}$ invertible. The linked theorem proves this assertion. For $b=\alpha=e^{-S/4}$ and $\beta=1$, choose $r_1<\Theta<r_2$. The resulting projection and invertibility give the clause in Lemma 4.5, while the geometric estimates provide additional quantitative information. The theorem applies to every such compact perturbation, independently of its origin as a fluid period map.
rows.name: Breakdown.dichotomyHolds
rows.plain: Finite-dimensional monodromy splitting with separated power bounds
rows.annotation: Lean states the backward estimate without introducing inverse notation: $\|P_{\mathrm u}x\|\le Kr_2^{-n}\|\mathcal M^nP_{\mathrm u}x\|$. Taking $n=1$ gives injectivity on the exterior range, and the separate surjectivity hypothesis gives an inverse there. Taking $P_{\mathrm u}x=\mathcal M_{\mathrm u}^{-n}y$ recovers the inverse-power bound. No inverse of the full operator is needed.

assessments.fidelity_note: Let $X$ be a real Hilbert space and $M=T_0+C$, where $T_0,C$ are bounded linear operators, $C$ is compact and $\|T_0\|\le b\le\alpha<\beta$ with $b\ge0$. The last two properties make the restricted operator $M_{\mathrm u}$ invertible. For $r_1<\Theta<r_2$, the first series in (4.11) is bounded by $K\sum_n(r_1/\Theta)^n$. On $\operatorname{ran}P$, the second inequality gives $\|M_{\mathrm u}^{-n}\|\le Kr_2^{-n}$, so the second series is at most $K\|P\|\sum_n(\Theta/r_2)^n$. The formal assertion gives these geometric bounds instead of merely summability. This linked item defines the assertion; its proof is a separate theorem.

A radius at which one had only bounded divided homogeneous powers would not suffice: summing $n$ equally sized divided source contributions can give growth proportional to $n$. ties.plain: Monodromy is a compact perturbation of free evolution

rows.plain: Monodromy is a compact perturbation of free evolution
rows.annotation: A free step is $B=D_\mu e^{(1-\mu)\Delta}$ with $\mu=e^{-S/k}$. The product law for the heat and dilation gives $B^k=D_{\mu^k}e^{(1-\mu^k)\Delta}$; its norm is at most $\mu^{k/4}=e^{-S/4}$. Thus subdivision of the period has not changed the free spectral bound. The final inverse isometry has norm one.

ties.name: Breakdown.DichotomyHolds
ties.plain: Finite-dimensional spectral splitting of a compact perturbation

rows.fidelity_note: Let $X$ be a real Hilbert space and $M=T_0+C$, where $T_0,C$ are bounded linear operators, $C$ is compact and $\|T_0\|\le b\le\alpha<\beta$ with $b\ge0$. The formal assertion supplies $\alpha<r_1<r_2<\beta$, $K>0$ and a bounded finite-rank projection $P$ such that $PM=MP$, $\|M^n(I-P)\|\le Kr_1^n$ and $\|Px\|\le Kr_2^{-n}\|M^nPx\|$ for all natural $n$ and $x\in X$; $M$ maps $\operatorname{ran}P$ onto itself. The last two properties make the restricted operator $M_{\mathrm u}$ invertible. The paper explicitly identifies the spectra of the restrictions to the interior and exterior spectral subspaces. The formal assertion records the two geometric bounds and surjectivity on $\operatorname{ran}P$; these yield an inverse there and the estimates used subsequently. It contains no equality identifying either restricted spectrum.
rows.name: Breakdown.DichotomyHolds
rows.plain: Finite-dimensional spectral splitting of a compact perturbation
rows.annotation: For the restriction to the interior, choose $r_1$ strictly between its spectral radius and $\Theta$; for the inverse restriction to the exterior choose $r_2^{-1}$ strictly between its spectral radius and $\Theta^{-1}$. The spectral radius formula bounds sufficiently large powers at these rates; finitely many earlier powers are absorbed into the constant. In particular the argument does not require the projections to be orthogonal or the operator to be normal.

ties.plain: Interval splitting and right-inverse data for the linearized equation

rows.fidelity_note: Let $X$ be a real Hilbert space. Suppose $G(t)$, $t\ge0$, is a strongly continuous contraction semigroup and $K(\tau)$ is a symmetric bounded bilinear family, continuous on each pair of arguments for $\tau>0$, with $G(s)K(\tau)=K(s+\tau)$ and $\|K(\tau)\|\le C_K\tau^{-3/4}$ for $0<\tau\le1$. For $\mu>0$, suppose the dilations are strongly continuous, $D_1=I$, $D_\mu D_\eta=D_{\mu\eta}$, $\|D_\mu x\|=\mu^{1/4}\|x\|$, $D_\mu G(\mu t)=G(t)D_\mu$ for $t\ge0$, and $\mu D_\mu K(\mu\tau)(x,y)=K(\tau)(D_\mu x,D_\mu y)$ for $\tau>0$. For a dense set of $f\in X$, require $K(\tau)(f,\cdot)$ compact for every $\tau>0$. Let $\rho$ be a surjective linear isometry commuting with $G,K,D$, including their assigned values at all real parameters. Let $S>0$ and let $w:\mathbb R\to X$ be continuous and nonzero somewhere, with $w(s+S)=\rho w(s)$. For $a\le s$, require the Bochner integral to exist and $w(s)=D_{e^{-(s-a)}}G(1-e^{-(s-a)})w(a)+\int_a^sD_{e^{-(s-r)}}K(1-e^{-(s-r)})(w(r),w(r))\,dr$. For a dense linear subspace $C\subset X$ and $t_0>0$, the formal assertion chooses $k\ge1$, $\mu=e^{-S/k}$, $L=1-\mu\le t_0$ and $\mu^{1/4}<\theta<1$. On $Y=C([0,L];X)$ with its supremum norm, set $a_n(t)=D_{(1-t)^{-1}}w(nS/k-\log(1-t))$, $A_nz(t)=2\int_0^tK(t-r)(a_n(r),z(r))\,dr$, $\Gamma x(t)=G(t)x$, and $Ev=D_\mu v(L)$. It gives $\|A_n\|\le1/4$, a finite-dimensional $V\subset X$, a bounded linear $J:X\to X$ with range in $C$, and a bounded linear $\mathcal R:\ell^\infty(Y)\to X\times\ell^\infty(Y)$. Writing $(e,z)=\mathcal Rg$, the conclusions are $e\in V$, $z_0-A_0z_0-\Gamma Je=g_0$ and $z_n-A_nz_n-\theta^{-1}\Gamma Ez_{n-1}=g_n$ for $n\ge1$. The physical datum correction is $Je\in J(V)$; its bound also uses $\|J\|$. The chosen short-interval weight satisfies $e^{-S/(4k)}<\theta<1$. rows.name: Breakdown.StepDataStatement
rows.plain: Interval splitting and right-inverse data for the linearized equation
rows.annotation: From $\Theta=\lambda^\kappa$ one has $\kappa=-\log\Theta/S$. The interval $\lambda^{1/4}<\Theta<1$ is exactly $0<\kappa<1/4$. If there are $k$ steps in one period, $\theta=\Theta^{1/k}$ is the decay weight per step and $\theta^k=\Theta$; one should not use the full-period weight on every short step.

rows.plain: A right inverse for the linearized equations on interval sequences
rows.annotation: The normalized reference on short interval $j$ is the physical solution started at phase $jS/k$. rows.fidelity_note: For a bounded linear operator $M$ on a real normed space, a real $\theta$, a prescribed source sequence $c_n$ and an initial value $x_0$, the formal definition is $x_{n+1}=\theta^{-1}(Mx_n+c_n)$ for natural $n$. It has no boundedness or decay conclusion. At $\theta=0$ division is assigned zero; the dichotomy arguments impose $\theta>0$. The source $c_n$ and the initial value $x_0$ are independent inputs to this definition. The paper claims that its particular endpoint forcing depends linearly on a global source and is independent of a prescribed initial datum. No map from that global source to $c_n$ is part of the formal definition, so the quoted independence and linearity are not its assertions.
rows.name: Breakdown.orbitSeq
rows.plain: Weighted monodromy recurrence with forcing
rows.annotation: The key point of the second identity in (4.14) is that $f_n$ is independent of $\chi_0$. Thus the datum can be chosen using the entire sequence of $f_n$, computed from the prescribed $g$. For the nonlinear equation we first fix a trial quadratic source, apply this linear selection, then use the resulting trajectory to update the source.

ties.name: Breakdown.PeriodicInverseStatement
ties.plain: A right inverse for the linearized equations on interval sequences

rows.fidelity_note: Let $X,Y$ be real Banach spaces, $k\ge1$, $\theta>0$, and let $\rho:X\to X$ be a surjective linear isometry. Let $A_n:Y\to Y$, $\Gamma:X\to Y$, $E:Y\to X$ and $J,P:X\to X$ be bounded linear maps. Assume $I-A_n$ have uniformly bounded inverses. Set $S_n=E(I-A_n)^{-1}\Gamma$ and $M=\rho^{-1}S_{k-1}\cdots S_0$, and assume $S_{n+k}=\rho S_n\rho^{-1}$, $P^2=P$, $PM=MP$, $PJ=P$. For $0\le r_1<\theta^k<r_2$, require $\|M^n(I-P)\|\le Kr_1^n$, $\|Px\|\le Kr_2^{-n}\|M^nPx\|$ for all $n\ge0,x\in X$, and surjectivity of $M$ on $\operatorname{ran}P$. The formal assertion supplies a bounded linear $\mathcal R:\ell^\infty(Y)\to X\times\ell^\infty(Y)$. For $(e,z)=\mathcal Rg$, it states $e\in\operatorname{ran}P$, $z_0-A_0z_0-\Gamma Je=g_0$ and $z_n-A_nz_n-\theta^{-1}\Gamma Ez_{n-1}=g_n$ for $n\ge1$. The product norm is $\max(\|e\|,\sup_n\|z_n\|_Y)$. The previous-endpoint term $\theta^{-1}\Gamma Ez_{n-1}$ is the formal recurrence coupling. The paper derives the specific continuous-time restart formula for $v-g$ by subtracting its Duhamel identities. The formal assertion takes the interval maps as inputs and does not prove that restart formula for a global forced curve.
rows.name: Breakdown.PeriodicInverseStatement
rows.plain: A right inverse for the linearized equations on interval sequences
rows.annotation: Splitting the integral at $t_n$ and using (3.12), the part before $t_n$ is the heat evolution of $2\mathcal B(u^*,v)(t_n)$. Adding the original heat term yields the heat evolution of $v(t_n)-g(t_n)$. The remaining integral begins at $t_n$; this is the exact restart identity even when $g$ has no time derivative.

ties.name: Breakdown.Freq.DilationAlgebra
ties.plain: Dilation of solenoidal fields

rows.fidelity_note: The formal space $X$ is a frequency-side model of $\dot H^1_{\mathrm{div}}(\mathbb R^3)$: a closed subspace of $L^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C^3)$ of transverse fields with the reality symmetry, on which $G(t)$ is the multiplier $e^{-4\pi^2t|\xi|^2}$ and $D_\mu$ acts by $f(\xi)\mapsto\mu^{-1/2}f(\xi/\sqrt\mu)$, the frequency form of $D_\mu u(x)=\sqrt\mu\,u(\sqrt\mu x)$. For $\mu,\eta>0$ the formal assertion states $\|D_\mu x\|=\mu^{1/4}\|x\|$, $D_1=I$, $D_\mu D_\eta=D_{\mu\eta}$, $D_\mu G(\mu t)=G(t)D_\mu$ for $t\ge0$, and agreement of $D_\mu$ with the dilation on $L^2$. For natural $n$, $\lambda=e^{-S}>0$ and $\sigma\ge0$, set $\mu=\lambda^n$ and $t=\sigma$ to obtain $D_{\lambda^n}G(\lambda^n\sigma)=G(\sigma)D_{\lambda^n}$. Commutation with $\rho_R$ and the identification of the rescaled initial vector are additional steps in the paper's equation. They are not components of this dilation assertion.
rows.name: Breakdown.Freq.DilationAlgebra
rows.plain: Dilation of solenoidal fields
rows.annotation: Writing $\mu=\lambda^n$, the identity $D_\mu e^{\mu\sigma\Delta}=e^{\sigma\Delta}D_\mu$ moves the normalized heat operator outside the change of coordinates. Together with commutation with the isometry, the incoming heat curve becomes $e^{\sigma\Delta}\chi_n$. There is no extra power of $\lambda$ in this term.

ties.name: Breakdown.MildFramework.stepOp
ties.plain: Linearized Duhamel operator on one orbit interval

rows.fidelity_note: Let $X$ be a real Hilbert space. Suppose $G(t)$, $t\ge0$, is a strongly continuous contraction semigroup and $K(\tau)$ is a symmetric bounded bilinear family, continuous on each pair of arguments for $\tau>0$, with $G(s)K(\tau)=K(s+\tau)$ and $\|K(\tau)\|\le C_K\tau^{-3/4}$ for $0<\tau\le1$. For $\mu>0$, suppose the dilations are strongly continuous, $D_1=I$, $D_\mu D_\eta=D_{\mu\eta}$, $\|D_\mu x\|=\mu^{1/4}\|x\|$, $D_\mu G(\mu t)=G(t)D_\mu$ for $t\ge0$, and $\mu D_\mu K(\mu\tau)(x,y)=K(\tau)(D_\mu x,D_\mu y)$ for $\tau>0$. For a dense set of $f\in X$, require $K(\tau)(f,\cdot)$ compact for every $\tau>0$. Let $\rho$ be a surjective linear isometry commuting with $G,K,D$, including their assigned values at all real parameters. Let $S>0$ and let $w:\mathbb R\to X$ be continuous and nonzero somewhere, with $w(s+S)=\rho w(s)$. For $a\le s$, require the Bochner integral to exist and $w(s)=D_{e^{-(s-a)}}G(1-e^{-(s-a)})w(a)+\int_a^sD_{e^{-(s-r)}}K(1-e^{-(s-r)})(w(r),w(r))\,dr$. For $k\ge1$ and $L=1-e^{-S/k}$, the formal interaction is $A_nv(t)=2\int_0^tK(t-r)(a_n(r),v(r))\,dr$, with $a_n(t)=D_{(1-t)^{-1}}w(nS/k-\log(1-t))$. The kernel-scaling identity is an assumption of the surrounding mathematical setting. The definition of $A_n$ does not itself assert the change of variables from a global forced solution or the whole-period formula printed here.
rows.name: Breakdown.MildFramework.stepOp
rows.plain: Linearized Duhamel operator on one orbit interval
rows.annotation: Upon setting $t'=t_n+\lambda^n\sigma'$, the factor $dt'=\lambda^n d\sigma'$ cancels the inverse time-scaling factor of $K$. In formulas, for $\mu=\lambda^n$, $\mu D_\mu K(\mu\tau)(a,b)=K(\tau)(D_\mu a,D_\mu b)$. Isometry equivariance and (4.3) then return the mixed kernel to $K(\sigma-\sigma')(u^*(\sigma'),v_n(\sigma'))$.

ties.name: Breakdown.stepMap
ties.plain: One-step linearized evolution from the interval inverse

rows.fidelity_note: For real normed spaces $X,Y$ and bounded linear maps $A_n:Y\to Y$, $\Gamma:X\to Y$, $E:Y\to X$, the formal definition is $S_n=E(I-A_n)^{-1}\Gamma$. An operator without a bounded inverse is assigned inverse zero. If $I-A_n$ is invertible, $(I-A_n)^{-1}\Gamma x$ solves the linear interval equation, and $S_nx$ is its rescaled endpoint. In the application $Y=C([0,L];X)$, $\Gamma x(t)=G(t)x$, and $Ev=D_\mu v(L)$. When $I-A_n$ is invertible, the corresponding interval trajectory with a source is $(I-A_n)^{-1}(\Gamma\chi+g)$. The formal definition here applies $E$ only to the homogeneous trajectory $(I-A_n)^{-1}\Gamma\chi$. It states neither the inhomogeneous trajectory identity nor the paper's unsplit decomposition on $[0,1-e^{-S}]$.
rows.name: Breakdown.stepMap
rows.plain: One-step linearized evolution from the interval inverse
rows.annotation: Linearity of $\mathcal U$ separates $v_n$ into the solution driven by the incoming heat datum and that driven by the local additive curve. The monodromy is obtained from the first part alone. The second part contributes the source response to the recurrence; it must not be included in the definition of the homogeneous step map.

ties.name: Breakdown.orbitSeq
ties.plain: Weighted monodromy recurrence with forcing

rows.fidelity_note: For a bounded linear operator $M$ on a real normed space, a real $\theta$, a prescribed source sequence $c_n$ and an initial value $x_0$, the formal definition is $x_{n+1}=\theta^{-1}(Mx_n+c_n)$ for natural $n$. It has no boundedness or decay conclusion. At $\theta=0$ division is assigned zero; the dichotomy arguments impose $\theta>0$. For $\theta>0$, set $\chi_n=\theta^nx_n$ and $f_n=\theta^nc_n$ to obtain the unweighted recurrence. The paper also gives a specific endpoint expression for $f_n$ using the full-period solution operator $\mathcal U$. The formal definition begins with a supplied sequence $c_n$ and contains no such endpoint formula.
rows.name: Breakdown.orbitSeq
rows.plain: Weighted monodromy recurrence with forcing
rows.annotation: At the common physical endpoint of periods $n$ and $n+1$ the two normalized values differ by $\rho_R^{-1}D_\lambda$. Applying this map to $v_n(t_1)-g_n(t_1)$ gives $\chi_{n+1}$. With $v_n=h_{\chi_n}+\mathcal U g_n$, its homogeneous term is $\mathcal M\chi_n$ and its source is precisely the difference in (4.13).

ties.name: Breakdown.exists_section
ties.plain: Lifting a finite-dimensional projection

rows.fidelity_note: Breakdown/Transfer/Section.lean constructs a linear section into any chosen dense submodule by lifting a basis of the range.
rows.name: Breakdown.exists_section
rows.note: Breakdown/Transfer/Section.lean constructs a linear section into any chosen dense submodule by lifting a basis of the range.
rows.plain: Lifting a finite-dimensional projection
rows.annotation: The lift is a bounded map on the finite-dimensional exterior range, and extending it by first applying $P_{\mathrm u}$ gives a map $J$ on $X$ satisfying $P_{\mathrm u}J=P_{\mathrm u}$. In the proof of `exists_section` this is the composition of `J₀` with the range restriction of the projection. The map $J$ selects a datum; it need not commute with $\mathcal M$.

ties.name: Breakdown.DiscreteDichotomyInternal.step_tailSum
ties.plain: The future tail satisfies the recurrence

rows.fidelity_note: Let $X$ be a real Banach space and $N,M,P:X\to X$ bounded and linear with $PN=N$ and $MN=P$. Assume $0<\Theta<r_2$, $A\ge0$, $\|N^{j+1}x\|\le Ar_2^{-j-1}\|x\|$ for every natural $j$ and $x\in X$, and $\|c_j\|\le R$ for all $j$, so that $U(c)=-\sum_{j\ge0}\Theta^jN^{j+1}c_j$ converges. The formal theorem proves $\Theta^{-1}(MU(c)+Pc_0)=U((c_{j+1})_{j\ge0})$. Iterating and restoring the normalization $f_j=\Theta^jc_j$ gives the future-tail form in the paper. This theorem does not identify $c_j$ with the source derived from a global solution, and it does not supply the complementary finite sum.
rows.name: Breakdown.DiscreteDichotomyInternal.step_tailSum
rows.plain: The future tail satisfies the recurrence
rows.annotation: Multiplication of the future sum at $n$ by $\mathcal M_{\mathrm u}$ gives a first term $-P_{\mathrm u}f_n$; adding the current forcing cancels it. All later summands have the exponents of the sum at $n+1$. This checks the recurrence itself, not only the bound on its solution.

rows.fidelity_note: Let $X$ be a real Banach space, $B:X\to X$ bounded and linear, and $w_n,d_n$ sequences satisfying $w_{n+1}=Bw_n+d_n$ for every natural $n$. The formal theorem proves $w_n=B^nw_0+\sum_{m<n}B^{n-1-m}d_m$. At $n=0$ the sum is empty; for $m<n$ the exponent $n-1-m$ is a nonnegative integer. Apply this with $w_n=(I-P_{\mathrm u})\chi_n$, $B=\mathcal M$ and $d_n=(I-P_{\mathrm u})f_n$, using commutation, to obtain the second identity. No infinite-series identity is concluded.
rows.name: Breakdown.DiscreteDichotomyInternal.rec_formula
rows.plain: The forward variation-of-constants sum
rows.annotation: The forward formula has a homogeneous term $\mathcal M^n(I-P_{\mathrm u})\gamma$ as well as the past sources. One must retain this term: the compact lift of the prescribed exterior datum need not itself lie in the exterior range. A source at index $m$ enters the state at $m+1$ and undergoes exactly $n-1-m$ further returns.

ties.name: Breakdown.DiscreteDichotomyStatement
ties.plain: A bounded forced recurrence

rows.fidelity_note: Let $X$ be a real Banach space, $M,P$ bounded linear operators with $P^2=P$ and $PM=MP$, and $0\le r_1<\Theta<r_2$. Assume $\|M^n(I-P)\|\le Kr_1^n$, $\|Px\|\le Kr_2^{-n}\|M^nPx\|$ for every natural $n$ and $x\in X$, and surjectivity of $M$ on $\operatorname{ran}P$. The formal assertion supplies a bounded linear $U:\ell^\infty(X)\to X$ with $PUc=Uc$ and a constant $K\prime$. If $Px_0=Uc$, the normalized recurrence $x_{n+1}=\Theta^{-1}(Mx_n+c_n)$ satisfies $\|x_n\|\le K\prime(\|x_0\|+\|c\|_\infty)$ for all $n$. Finite rank of $P$ is not assumed here. For $\chi_n=\Theta^nx_n$ and $f_n=\Theta^nc_n$, the uniform formal bound becomes geometric decay in $n$. The paper derives that decay from the two series in (4.11). The formal assertion instead assumes forward and inverse geometric bounds at the two radii and works directly with a bounded normalized source sequence.
rows.name: Breakdown.DiscreteDichotomyStatement
rows.plain: A bounded forced recurrence
rows.annotation: The estimate for past forcing is $KF\Theta^n/(\Theta-r_1)$, and that for future forcing is $AF\Theta^n/(r_2-\Theta)$, if $\|f_m\|\le F\Theta^m$ and the two projected power bounds have constants $K,A$. For the past sum the exponent of a power is $n-1-m$; for the future sum the inverse exponent is $m-n+1$. The remaining homogeneous term has norm at most $Kr_1^n\|\gamma\|$.

ties.name: Breakdown.PeriodicInverseStatement
ties.plain: A right inverse for the linearized equations on interval sequences

Set $S_n=E(I-A_n)^{-1}\Gamma$ and $M=\rho^{-1}S_{k-1}\cdots S_0$, and assume $S_{n+k}=\rho S_n\rho^{-1}$, $P^2=P$, $PM=MP$, $PJ=P$. For $0\le r_1<\theta^k<r_2$, require $\|M^n(I-P)\|\le Kr_1^n$, $\|Px\|\le Kr_2^{-n}\|M^nPx\|$ for all $n\ge0,x\in X$, and surjectivity of $M$ on $\operatorname{ran}P$. That global source norm and the whole-period estimate are not named in the formal assertion.
rows.name: Breakdown.PeriodicInverseStatement
rows.plain: A right inverse for the linearized equations on interval sequences
rows.annotation: The decay of the endpoint $\chi_n$ must be converted to a bound on the whole normalized period. Use $v_n=\mathcal U(e^{\sigma\Delta}\chi_n+g_n)$ and heat contractivity to obtain $\|v_n\|_\infty\le\|\mathcal U\|(\|\chi_n\|+\|g_n\|_\infty)$. This step has one fixed constant for all periods, so it loses no decay rate.

ties.name: Breakdown.MildFramework.gluePieces
ties.plain: Joining rescaled time intervals

rows.fidelity_note: For $0<\mu<1$ and continuous curves $a_n:[0,1-\mu]\to X$ in a real Hilbert space with dilations $D_\mu$, the formal reconstruction is $v(t)=D_{\mu^{-n}}a_n(\sigma)$, $n=\lfloor\log(1-t)/\log\mu\rfloor_{\mathbb N}$ and $\sigma=(t-(1-\mu^n))/\mu^n$. On $0\le t<1$ this gives $0\le\sigma<1-\mu$ and $1-t=\mu^n(1-\sigma)$. The natural-number floor is zero on negative inputs. Outside each interval a curve is extended by its endpoint value. If the dilation law is $\|D_\eta x\|=\eta^{1/4}\|x\|$ for $\eta>0$, then $\|v(t)\|=\mu^{-n/4}\|a_n(\sigma)\|$. A separate bound $\|a_n\|\lesssim\theta^n$ and a choice $\theta=\mu^\kappa$ give the type of weighted rate used in the paper. The reconstruction definition supplies no such sequence estimate or bound in the global $C_\kappa$ norm.
rows.name: Breakdown.MildFramework.gluePieces
rows.plain: Joining rescaled time intervals
rows.annotation: Undoing the change of scale gives the exact norm relation $(1-t)^{1/4-\kappa}\|v(t)\|_X=(1-\sigma)^{1/4-\kappa}\Theta^{-n}\|v_n(\sigma)\|_X$. The phase factor is at most one and at least $\lambda^{1/4-\kappa}$ on a period. Thus bounded divided pieces give the claimed physical-time estimate, and conversely the physical-time estimate bounds all divided pieces.

ties.name: Breakdown.StepDataStatement
ties.plain: Interval splitting and right-inverse data for the linearized equation

For $\mu>0$, suppose the dilations are strongly continuous, $D_1=I$, $D_\mu D_\eta=D_{\mu\eta}$, $\|D_\mu x\|=\mu^{1/4}\|x\|$, $D_\mu G(\mu t)=G(t)D_\mu$ for $t\ge0$, and $\mu D_\mu K(\mu\tau)(x,y)=K(\tau)(D_\mu x,D_\mu y)$ for $\tau>0$. For a dense set of $f\in X$, require $K(\tau)(f,\cdot)$ compact for every $\tau>0$. Let $\rho$ be a surjective linear isometry commuting with $G,K,D$, including their assigned values at all real parameters. Let $S>0$ and let $w:\mathbb R\to X$ be continuous and nonzero somewhere, with $w(s+S)=\rho w(s)$. That curve must be reconstructed and its weighted estimate proved; neither is a stated conclusion of this sequence assertion.
rows.name: Breakdown.StepDataStatement
rows.plain: Interval splitting and right-inverse data for the linearized equation
rows.annotation: For this fixed choice of $E$, the linear inverse (4.8) is in fact unique. The difference of two solutions has zero source and initial datum in $E$. Its exterior projection must vanish by the backward power bound, whence the datum is zero because $E\cap\ker P_{\mathrm u}=\{0\}$. Local uniqueness gives zero trajectory. The resulting linear map is bounded by the preceding estimates.

rows.fidelity_note: Let $X,Y$ be real Banach spaces, $k\ge1$, $\theta>0$, and let $\rho:X\to X$ be a surjective linear isometry. Let $A_n:Y\to Y$, $\Gamma:X\to Y$, $E:Y\to X$ and $J,P:X\to X$ be bounded linear maps. Assume $I-A_n$ have uniformly bounded inverses. Set $S_n=E(I-A_n)^{-1}\Gamma$ and $M=\rho^{-1}S_{k-1}\cdots S_0$, and assume $S_{n+k}=\rho S_n\rho^{-1}$, $P^2=P$, $PM=MP$, $PJ=P$. rows.name: Breakdown.PeriodicInverseStatement
rows.plain: A right inverse for the linearized equations on interval sequences
rows.annotation: In the sequence inverse the first component is an exterior vector; applying the fixed lift makes it a physical datum correction. Its second component solves the local equations for arbitrary additive curves. Matching the full endpoints also requires the local sources to vanish at each noninitial left endpoint; the residual and quadratic Duhamel term have this property in the nonlinear application. Thus the gluing assertion concerns the corrected mild trajectory, not arbitrary inputs to the abstract inverse.

ties.name: Breakdown.HeatBilinear
ties.plain: Heat and bilinear evolution assumptions

rows.fidelity_note: The formal data consist of a real normed space $X$, operators $G(t)$ defined for all real $t$ with $G(0)=I$, the semigroup law and strong continuity for $t\ge0$, and $\|G(t)\|\le1$ there. They also include symmetric bilinear maps $K(\tau)$, continuous on each pair for $\tau>0$, with $G(s)K(\tau)=K(s+\tau)$ for $s\ge0,\tau>0$ and $\|K(\tau)\|\le C_K\tau^{-3/4}$ for $0<\tau\le1$. The kernel bound is assumed only for $0<\tau\le1$, while (3.12) assumes it for all $\tau>0$. The paper's abstract setting assumes $X$ is Banach. Completeness is not part of this formal data definition; it is imposed in the integral and correction statements. This definition supplies the common operator assumptions, without itself proving either nonlinear lemma.
rows.name: Breakdown.HeatBilinear
rows.plain: Heat and bilinear evolution assumptions
rows.annotation: The construction of the torus inverse is postponed to Section 6; the contraction uses only its trajectory estimate, as in (4.22). Neither compactness of the kernel nor the spectral splitting is required again here. This separation allows the same lemma to correct an approximate field that is not recurrent on the torus.

ties.name: Breakdown.Periodic.SeqPerturbation
ties.plain: Correcting a periodic approximate flow on all time intervals

rows.fidelity_note: Let $X,E$ be real Banach spaces, $0<L\le1$, $0<\theta<1$, $c\in\mathbb R$, and $C_K\ge0$. For each $n$, suppose $G_n$ is a strongly continuous contraction semigroup and $K_n$ is a symmetric bounded bilinear family, continuous for positive lag, with $G_n(s)K_n(\tau)=K_n(s+\tau)$ for $s\ge0,\tau>0$ and $\|K_n(\tau)\|\le C_K\tau^{-3/4}$ for $0<\tau\le1$. On $Y=C([0,L];X)$ put $B_n(f,g)(t)=\int_0^tK_n(t-r)(f(r),g(r))\,dr$ and $\Gamma_nx(t)=G_n(t)x$. Assume $a_n,r_n\in Y$, $\sup_n\|a_n\|_Y<\infty$, $a_n=\Gamma_na_n(0)+B_n(a_n,a_n)+r_n$, $\|r_n\|_Y\le\theta^n\rho$, and $a_{n+1}(0)=c\,a_n(L)$. For bounded linear $J:E\to X$, require a bounded linear $\mathcal R:\ell^\infty(Y)\to E\times\ell^\infty(Y)$ which sends $g$ to $(e,z)$ satisfying $z_0-2B_0(a_0,z_0)-\Gamma_0Je=g_0$ and $z_n-2B_n(a_n,z_n)-(c/\theta)\Gamma_nz_{n-1}(L)=g_n$ for $n\ge1$. If $\xi\in X$ obeys $64\|\mathcal R\|^2C_KL^{1/4}(\rho+\|\xi\|)\le1$, the formal assertion supplies $e$ and $z_n$ with $\max(\|e\|,\sup_n\|z_n\|_Y)\le2\|\mathcal R\|(\rho+\|\xi\|)$. The curves $v_n=a_n+\theta^nz_n$ are exact mild solutions on $[0,L]$, $v_{n+1}(0)=c\,v_n(L)$ and $z_0(0)=\xi+Je$. The paper's (4.16) defines one global residual $F^{\mathrm a}$ and one global linear map $\mathcal L$. The formal assertion uses the residuals $r_n$ and coupled linear equations on a sequence of compact intervals, with an endpoint term after the first interval. It is a conditional correction assertion, not a definition of the two global expressions.
rows.name: Breakdown.Periodic.SeqPerturbation
rows.plain: Correcting a periodic approximate flow on all time intervals
rows.annotation: The residual is the difference between the proposed curve and the mild formula with its own initial value. It is zero at the left endpoint whether or not the curve solves the equation. The sign in (4.17) is negative because the error must cancel this defect; in the piece version this also makes the residual contribution zero at each restart.

ties.name: Breakdown.Periodic.SeqPerturbation
ties.plain: Correcting a periodic approximate flow on all time intervals

rows.fidelity_note: Let $X,E$ be real Banach spaces, $0<L\le1$, $0<\theta<1$, $c\in\mathbb R$, and $C_K\ge0$. For each $n$, suppose $G_n$ is a strongly continuous contraction semigroup and $K_n$ is a symmetric bounded bilinear family, continuous for positive lag, with $G_n(s)K_n(\tau)=K_n(s+\tau)$ for $s\ge0,\tau>0$ and $\|K_n(\tau)\|\le C_K\tau^{-3/4}$ for $0<\tau\le1$. On $Y=C([0,L];X)$ put $B_n(f,g)(t)=\int_0^tK_n(t-r)(f(r),g(r))\,dr$ and $\Gamma_nx(t)=G_n(t)x$. Assume $a_n,r_n\in Y$, $\sup_n\|a_n\|_Y<\infty$, $a_n=\Gamma_na_n(0)+B_n(a_n,a_n)+r_n$, $\|r_n\|_Y\le\theta^n\rho$, and $a_{n+1}(0)=c\,a_n(L)$. For bounded linear $J:E\to X$, require a bounded linear $\mathcal R:\ell^\infty(Y)\to E\times\ell^\infty(Y)$ which sends $g$ to $(e,z)$ satisfying $z_0-2B_0(a_0,z_0)-\Gamma_0Je=g_0$ and $z_n-2B_n(a_n,z_n)-(c/\theta)\Gamma_nz_{n-1}(L)=g_n$ for $n\ge1$. If $\xi\in X$ obeys $64\|\mathcal R\|^2C_KL^{1/4}(\rho+\|\xi\|)\le1$, the formal assertion supplies $e$ and $z_n$ with $\max(\|e\|,\sup_n\|z_n\|_Y)\le2\|\mathcal R\|(\rho+\|\xi\|)$. The curves $v_n=a_n+\theta^nz_n$ are exact mild solutions on $[0,L]$, $v_{n+1}(0)=c\,v_n(L)$ and $z_0(0)=\xi+Je$. The residual hypothesis is $a_n=\Gamma_na_n(0)+B_n(a_n,a_n)+r_n$. If $r_n=0$, this is precisely the mild identity on that closed interval; continuity and integrability follow from the interval setting. The paper states an equivalence for a single curve on $[0,1)$. This linked assertion does not state that global equivalence.
rows.name: Breakdown.Periodic.SeqPerturbation
rows.plain: Correcting a periodic approximate flow on all time intervals
rows.annotation: The defect in (4.16) is a mild-equation residual, so its norm is measured after the heat evolution and time integration, in the same space as the velocity error. This is the norm estimated in Lemma 6.2. In the formal sequence setting the analogous local defect is divided by $\theta^n$; its smallness is a bound uniform in $n$.

ties.name: Breakdown.PiecePerturbationStatement
ties.plain: Mild equation for an approximate flow plus a correction

rows.fidelity_note: Let $X$ be a real Banach space, $G(t)$ a strongly continuous contraction semigroup for $t\ge0$, and $K(\tau):X\times X\to X$ symmetric bounded bilinear maps. Assume $K(\tau)(f,g)$ depends continuously on $\tau>0$, $G(s)K(\tau)(f,g)=K(s+\tau)(f,g)$ for $s\ge0$, $\tau>0$, and $\|K(\tau)\|\le C_K\tau^{-3/4}$ for $0<\tau\le1$. Let $0<T\le1$, $a,v\in C([0,T];X)$ and $x\in X$. Write $B_T(f,g)(t)=\int_0^tK(t-r)(f(r),g(r))\,dr$. If $a(t)=G(t)a(0)+B_T(a,a)(t)$ and $v(t)=G(t)x+2B_T(a,v)(t)+B_T(v,v)(t)$, the formal assertion concludes $v(0)=x$ and $a+v$ is a continuous mild solution on $[0,T]$, including integrability of its Duhamel term. The formal assertion uses an exact background $a$ and the implication from its perturbation identity to a mild solution. The paper displays an algebraic identity valid for an arbitrary approximate background and an independent datum displacement. The residual term of that identity is absent from the formal perturbation statement.
rows.name: Breakdown.PiecePerturbationStatement
rows.plain: Mild equation for an approximate flow plus a correction
rows.annotation: Expanding $\mathcal B(u^{\mathrm a}+v,u^{\mathrm a}+v)$ gives the reference term, two equal mixed terms and the quadratic error. Subtracting the heat input of the prescribed datum separates $F^{\mathrm a}$ and $\mathcal L(\gamma,v)$ from the remaining two terms. For an exact background this reduces to the compact-interval implication `PiecePerturbationStatement`.

rows.name: Breakdown.Periodic.SeqPerturbation
rows.plain: Correcting a periodic approximate flow on all time intervals
rows.annotation: On piece $n$ write the actual normalized error as $\theta^nz_n$. Its quadratic term after division is $\theta^n N_n(z_n,z_n)$, while the given residual is $-\theta^{-n}r_n$. The prescribed datum contributes a heat curve on piece zero only. Later heat curves are those of the propagated corrected endpoints, so the initial perturbation is not counted again.

ties.name: Breakdown.ContractionInternal.exists_small_fixed
ties.plain: A quadratic contraction has a fixed point of norm at most 2b

rows.fidelity_note: Let $Z$ be a complete normed abelian group, $\Phi:Z\to Z$, and $b,K\ge0$ with $8Kb\le1$. The formal theorem assumes $\|\Phi(z)\|\le b+K\|z\|^2$ for every $z$ and $\|\Phi(z)-\Phi(w)\|\le K(\|z\|+\|w\|)\|z-w\|$ for every $z,w$. It proves that some $z$ satisfies $\Phi(z)=z$ and $\|z\|\le2b$. To use this theorem in the paper, $Z$ must be its complete weighted curve space and $\Phi$ the second component of the right-inverse image of the quadratic expression. Establishing the weighted Duhamel bounds is a separate step; they are not proved by this fixed-point theorem.
rows.name: Breakdown.ContractionInternal.exists_small_fixed
rows.plain: A quadratic contraction has a fixed point of norm at most 2b
rows.annotation: The contraction treats $e^{t\Delta}\chi-F^{\mathrm a}$ as a known curve and $\mathcal B(v,v)$ as a trial-dependent one. A linear inverse bound $C_{\mathcal R}$ makes the trial ball of radius twice the norm bound for the known response. The quadratic term is small relative to this radius when the known source is sufficiently small; no smallness of the mixed term is assumed.

ties.name: Breakdown.varConstIntegral
ties.plain: Continuity and bounds for Duhamel terms

rows.fidelity_note: Let $X$ be a real Banach space, $G(t)$ a strongly continuous contraction semigroup for $t\ge0$, and $K(\tau):X\times X\to X$ symmetric bounded bilinear maps. Assume $K(\tau)(f,g)$ depends continuously on $\tau>0$, $G(s)K(\tau)(f,g)=K(s+\tau)(f,g)$ for $s\ge0$, $\tau>0$, and $\|K(\tau)\|\le C_K\tau^{-3/4}$ for $0<\tau\le1$. For $a\le b$ and continuous $f,g:[a,b]\to X$ with $\|f(s)\|\le M$, $\|g(s)\|\le N$, the formal theorem proves that $B(f,g)(t)=\int_a^tK(t-r)(f(r),g(r))\,dr$ exists and is continuous on $[a,b]$. If $t-a\le1$, then $\|B(f,g)(t)\|\le4C_K(t-a)^{1/4}MN$. The formal conclusion uses constant bounds $M,N$ on a compact interval. Equation (4.18) instead integrates the singular factor against the time weight $(1-t\prime)^{\kappa-1/2}$ and identifies a constant by an integral over $(0,\infty)$. Neither that substitution nor that weighted estimate is stated by the linked theorem.
rows.name: Breakdown.varConstIntegral
rows.plain: Continuity and bounds for Duhamel terms
rows.annotation: Write $r=1-t$ and $\tau=t-t'$. Then $1-t'=r+\tau$, and the change $\tau=r\theta$ yields the factor $r^{-3/4+\kappa-1/2+1}=r^{\kappa-1/4}$. The remaining dimensionless integral is bounded independently of $t$; this is precisely the factor canceled by the weight of $C_\kappa$.

rows.fidelity_note: Let $X$ be a real Banach space, $G(t)$ a strongly continuous contraction semigroup for $t\ge0$, and $K(\tau):X\times X\to X$ symmetric bounded bilinear maps. Assume $K(\tau)(f,g)$ depends continuously on $\tau>0$, $G(s)K(\tau)(f,g)=K(s+\tau)(f,g)$ for $s\ge0$, $\tau>0$, and $\|K(\tau)\|\le C_K\tau^{-3/4}$ for $0<\tau\le1$. If $t-a\le1$, then $\|B(f,g)(t)\|\le4C_K(t-a)^{1/4}MN$. For continuous curves on $[0,1)$, each restriction to $[0,b]$, $b<1$, is bounded, so this theorem gives the continuity part of Lemma 4.7. The lemma also asserts a single constant depending only on $\kappa,C_K$ for its global weighted estimates. The formal theorem has no global weighted norm or such constant.
rows.name: Breakdown.varConstIntegral
rows.plain: Continuity and bounds for Duhamel terms
rows.annotation: The two products have different time dependence: the quadratic product has exponent $2\kappa-1/2$, and the interaction of a bounded field with a $C_0$ field has exponent $-1/4$. On $0<1-t'\le1$ both are bounded by $(1-t')^{\kappa-1/2}$. The common integral (4.18) therefore controls both (4.19) and the cutoff estimate (4.21).

rows.fidelity_note: Let $X$ be a real Banach space, $G(t)$ a strongly continuous contraction semigroup for $t\ge0$, and $K(\tau):X\times X\to X$ symmetric bounded bilinear maps. Assume $K(\tau)(f,g)$ depends continuously on $\tau>0$, $G(s)K(\tau)(f,g)=K(s+\tau)(f,g)$ for $s\ge0$, $\tau>0$, and $\|K(\tau)\|\le C_K\tau^{-3/4}$ for $0<\tau\le1$. For $T>0$, the formal assertion specifies $B_T(f,g)(t)=\int_0^tK(t-r)(f(r),g(r))\,dr$ and $\Gamma_Tx(t)=G(t)x$ on $C([0,T];X)$, with $\|\Gamma_T\|\le1$ and $\|B_T\|\le4C_KT^{1/4}$ when $T\le1$. All curve norms here are unweighted supremum norms. The paper's Lemma 4.7 concerns global norms on $[0,1)$ and includes a mixed estimate with one input in $C_0$. The formal assertion concerns the unweighted supremum norm on $[0,T]$, with the explicit factor $4C_KT^{1/4}$. It does not assert those global estimates or their common $\kappa$-dependent constant.
rows.name: Breakdown.PieceOperatorStatement
rows.plain: Uniform bounds for the Duhamel operator on a compact time interval
rows.annotation: On a compact interval the kernel estimate gives the factor $4C_KL^{1/4}$ times two ordinary supremum norms. These norms need not be bounded as the interval approaches time one. Substitution in (4.18) keeps the pointwise time-dependent input powers inside the integral and gives an output bound uniform in the weighted norm.

rows.name: Breakdown.PieceOperatorStatement
rows.plain: Uniform bounds for the Duhamel operator on a compact time interval
rows.annotation: The estimate loses some of the decay of a product of two errors: their product has the power $(1-t')^{2\kappa-1/2}$. In fact (4.18) with $\eta$ in place of $\kappa$ bounds $\mathcal B(v,v')$ in $C_\eta$ whenever $\eta\le2\kappa$ and $0<\eta<1/4$. For the fixed point it is enough to take $\eta=\kappa$, without changing the spectral circle used for the inverse.

ties.name: Breakdown.HeatBilinear
ties.plain: Heat and bilinear evolution assumptions

assessments.fidelity_note: For a real normed space $X$, the formal heat-flow condition requires bounded linear $G(t)$ with $G(0)=I$, the semigroup law, strong continuity for $t\ge0$, and $\|G(t)\|\le1$ for every $t\ge0$. The compared component is the contraction inequality $\|G(t)\chi\|\le\|\chi\|$. For $0<\kappa<1/4$ and $0\le t<1$, $(1-t)^{1/4-\kappa}\le1$, so taking the weighted supremum yields exactly (4.20). The formal hypothesis gives a stronger pointwise bound on the whole nonnegative time axis; it is an assumed property of the heat operators.

The formal heat assumption gives the unweighted bound $\|G(t)\chi\|\le\|\chi\|$ for every $t\ge0$. On $0\le t<1$ the factor $(1-t)^{1/4-\kappa}$ is at most one, so this implies the displayed weighted estimate.

rows.name: Breakdown.HeatBilinear
rows.plain: Heat and bilinear evolution assumptions
rows.annotation: By heat contractivity and $(1-t)^{1/4-\kappa}\le1$, the weighted norm of the heat curve is at most $\|\chi\|_X$. The value at $t=0$ attains this bound, so in fact equality holds. This is why smallness of the prescribed datum in $X$ suffices to make its heat input small in $C_\kappa$.

rows.fidelity_note: Let $X$ be a real Banach space, $G(t)$ a strongly continuous contraction semigroup for $t\ge0$, and $K(\tau):X\times X\to X$ symmetric bounded bilinear maps. Assume $K(\tau)(f,g)$ depends continuously on $\tau>0$, $G(s)K(\tau)(f,g)=K(s+\tau)(f,g)$ for $s\ge0$, $\tau>0$, and $\|K(\tau)\|\le C_K\tau^{-3/4}$ for $0<\tau\le1$. If $t-a\le1$, then $\|B(f,g)(t)\|\le4C_K(t-a)^{1/4}MN$. A constant bound for $g$ on a compact interval depends on its right endpoint and does not by itself state that global estimate. No exact counterpart of (4.21) occurs in the linked formal statement.
rows.name: Breakdown.varConstIntegral
rows.plain: Continuity and bounds for Duhamel terms
rows.annotation: The bounded input in (4.21) need not decay in physical time. In Section 6 it is the difference $\bar u-u^*$, whose ordinary supremum norm is $O(L^{-1/2})$ by (6.4). The other factor is allowed the reference rate in $C_0$. This estimate makes their mixed Duhamel term small in the stronger $C_\kappa$ norm required by the inverse.

rows.fidelity_note: Let $X$ be a real Banach space, $G(t)$ a strongly continuous contraction semigroup for $t\ge0$, and $K(\tau):X\times X\to X$ symmetric bounded bilinear maps. Assume $K(\tau)(f,g)$ depends continuously on $\tau>0$, $G(s)K(\tau)(f,g)=K(s+\tau)(f,g)$ for $s\ge0$, $\tau>0$, and $\|K(\tau)\|\le C_K\tau^{-3/4}$ for $0<\tau\le1$. If $t-a\le1$, then $\|B(f,g)(t)\|\le4C_K(t-a)^{1/4}MN$. Each continuous input curve on $[0,1)$ is bounded on every $[0,b]$ with $b<1$. Applying this formal continuity conclusion to those restrictions proves continuity at every time before one, exactly the compact-interval argument in the paper. No weighted norm estimate is needed for this continuity component.
rows.name: Breakdown.varConstIntegral
rows.plain: Continuity and bounds for Duhamel terms
rows.annotation: Fix $b<1$. Both inputs have finite ordinary supremum norms on $[0,b]$, so removing a lag shorter than $\varepsilon$ costs $O(\varepsilon^{1/4})$ uniformly there. The truncated integral varies continuously with its endpoint; passing to the limit proves continuity on $[0,b]$. Since $b$ is arbitrary, no field at time one is needed.

ties.plain: Heat and bilinear evolution assumptions

rows.fidelity_note: For a real normed space $X$, the formal kernel data include symmetric bounded bilinear $K(\tau)$ with $\|K(\tau)\|\le C_K\tau^{-3/4}$ for $0<\tau\le1$. Taking $\tau=t-t'$ for $0\le t'<t<1$ gives the first inequality in the paper's sentence. The subsequent estimates use the separate global definitions $\|v\|_\kappa=\sup_{s<1}(1-s)^{1/4-\kappa}\|v(s)\|$ and $\|g\|_0=\sup_{s<1}(1-s)^{1/4}\|g(s)\|$. Those norms and estimates are not part of the formal kernel data.
rows.name: Breakdown.HeatBilinear
rows.plain: Heat and bilinear evolution assumptions
rows.annotation: The lag $t-t'$ controls smoothing, while the time to the singularity $1-t'$ controls the size of the inputs. Their relation is $1-t'=(1-t)+(t-t')$. The substitution in (4.18) separates out the current remaining time $1-t$ and leaves a dimensionless integral, whose finiteness is what makes the bound uniform in $t$.

ties.name: Breakdown.PieceOperatorStatement
ties.plain: Uniform bounds for the Duhamel operator on a compact time interval

rows.fidelity_note: Let $X$ be a real Banach space, $G(t)$ a strongly continuous contraction semigroup for $t\ge0$, and $K(\tau):X\times X\to X$ symmetric bounded bilinear maps. Assume $K(\tau)(f,g)$ depends continuously on $\tau>0$, $G(s)K(\tau)(f,g)=K(s+\tau)(f,g)$ for $s\ge0$, $\tau>0$, and $\|K(\tau)\|\le C_K\tau^{-3/4}$ for $0<\tau\le1$. For $T>0$, the formal assertion specifies $B_T(f,g)(t)=\int_0^tK(t-r)(f(r),g(r))\,dr$ and $\Gamma_Tx(t)=G(t)x$ on $C([0,T];X)$, with $\|\Gamma_T\|\le1$ and $\|B_T\|\le4C_KT^{1/4}$ when $T\le1$. All curve norms here are unweighted supremum norms. The explicit constant in the formal compact-interval bound is $4C_KT^{1/4}$. The paper compares the powers $2\kappa-1/2$ and $-1/4$ with $\kappa-1/2$ on $0<1-t'\le1$, then uses the integral in (4.18). Those exponent comparisons, that improper-integral constant and the resulting global weighted bounds are absent from the linked assertion.
rows.name: Breakdown.PieceOperatorStatement
rows.plain: Uniform bounds for the Duhamel operator on a compact time interval
rows.annotation: At a fixed short interval the kernel gives a bound by $4C_K L^{1/4}$ times the two supremum norms. The global proof must instead keep the powers of $1-t'$ inside the time integral; a supremum over all physical times could be infinite. The rescaled piece proof handles the same issue by keeping the factor $\theta^n$ in its quadratic term.

rows.fidelity_note: The formal heat-flow assumption on a real normed space is $\|G(t)\|\le1$ for every $t\ge0$, with $G(0)=I$ and strong continuity. For $0<\kappa<1/4$ and $\chi\in X$, multiplication by $(1-t)^{1/4-\kappa}\le1$ on $[0,1)$ yields $\sup_{t<1}(1-t)^{1/4-\kappa}\|G(t)\chi\|\le\|\chi\|$, which is the final assertion (4.20). The other weighted bilinear estimates in the quoted passage do not follow from this assumption alone.
rows.name: Breakdown.HeatBilinear
rows.plain: Heat and bilinear evolution assumptions
rows.annotation: Only the heat contraction and the singular bilinear kernel bound are used here. These are the relevant fields of `HeatBilinear`. No recurrence or compactness is required for the nonlinear estimates once a bounded right inverse has been supplied.

ties.name: Breakdown.Periodic.SeqPerturbation
ties.plain: Correcting a periodic approximate flow on all time intervals

rows.fidelity_note: Let $X,E$ be real Banach spaces, $0<L\le1$, $0<\theta<1$, $c\in\mathbb R$, and $C_K\ge0$. For each $n$, suppose $G_n$ is a strongly continuous contraction semigroup and $K_n$ is a symmetric bounded bilinear family, continuous for positive lag, with $G_n(s)K_n(\tau)=K_n(s+\tau)$ for $s\ge0,\tau>0$ and $\|K_n(\tau)\|\le C_K\tau^{-3/4}$ for $0<\tau\le1$. On $Y=C([0,L];X)$ put $B_n(f,g)(t)=\int_0^tK_n(t-r)(f(r),g(r))\,dr$ and $\Gamma_nx(t)=G_n(t)x$. Assume $a_n,r_n\in Y$, $\sup_n\|a_n\|_Y<\infty$, $a_n=\Gamma_na_n(0)+B_n(a_n,a_n)+r_n$, $\|r_n\|_Y\le\theta^n\rho$, and $a_{n+1}(0)=c\,a_n(L)$. For bounded linear $J:E\to X$, require a bounded linear $\mathcal R:\ell^\infty(Y)\to E\times\ell^\infty(Y)$ which sends $g$ to $(e,z)$ satisfying $z_0-2B_0(a_0,z_0)-\Gamma_0Je=g_0$ and $z_n-2B_n(a_n,z_n)-(c/\theta)\Gamma_nz_{n-1}(L)=g_n$ for $n\ge1$. If $\xi\in X$ obeys $64\|\mathcal R\|^2C_KL^{1/4}(\rho+\|\xi\|)\le1$, the formal assertion supplies $e$ and $z_n$ with $\max(\|e\|,\sup_n\|z_n\|_Y)\le2\|\mathcal R\|(\rho+\|\xi\|)$. The curves $v_n=a_n+\theta^nz_n$ are exact mild solutions on $[0,L]$, $v_{n+1}(0)=c\,v_n(L)$ and $z_0(0)=\xi+Je$. The formal assertion requires a normed complete correction space $E$ and a bounded inverse controlling both components. In Lemma 4.8, $E$ is only a vector space and the bound is imposed on the curve component alone. The formal source norm also separates residual and datum displacement. These differences prevent identification of this assertion with the full global lemma.
rows.name: Breakdown.Periodic.SeqPerturbation
rows.plain: Correcting a periodic approximate flow on all time intervals
rows.annotation: The lemma assumes a right inverse of the mixed equation about the chosen reference, whether or not the reference is exact. It does not need that reference to be small. In `SeqPerturbation` the analogous given inverse acts on divided pieces, and the residual and prescribed heat input are small together. The hard part on the torus is constructing that inverse, not proving a second contraction principle.

rows.fidelity_note: For real Banach spaces $X,Y$, bounded linear $A_n:Y\to Y$, $\Gamma:X\to Y$, $E:Y\to X$, $J:X\to X$, a bounded bilinear $N:Y\times Y\to Y$, and $0<\theta\le1$, the formal assertion assumes a bounded linear inverse $\mathcal R$ for $z_0-A_0z_0-\Gamma Je=g_0$ and $z_n-A_nz_n-\theta^{-1}\Gamma Ez_{n-1}=g_n$. It then supplies $\varrho_0>0,C_1$ such that each $\|\xi\|\le\varrho_0$ admits $e$ and bounded $z$ with $\|e\|\le C_1\|\xi\|$ and the same equations with $\Gamma(Je+\xi)$ in the first row and $\theta^nN(z_n,z_n)$ on the right. This is the small-datum, zero-residual sequence correction. Lemma 4.8 permits an independent approximate residual and is stated for a global weighted curve.
rows.name: Breakdown.ContractionStatement
rows.plain: Small solution of the discrete quadratic correction equation
rows.annotation: For an exact reference the residual is zero. The source of the sequence inverse is $\Gamma\xi$ on the first interval, plus $\theta^nN(z_n,z_n)$ on every interval. The heat effect of $\xi$ is carried into later intervals by the preceding endpoints. The approximate-reference theorem adds the negative divided residual on each interval.

Set $S_n=E(I-A_n)^{-1}\Gamma$ and $M=\rho^{-1}S_{k-1}\cdots S_0$, and assume $S_{n+k}=\rho S_n\rho^{-1}$, $P^2=P$, $PM=MP$, $PJ=P$. For $0\le r_1<\theta^k<r_2$, require $\|M^n(I-P)\|\le Kr_1^n$, $\|Px\|\le Kr_2^{-n}\|M^nPx\|$ for all $n\ge0,x\in X$, and surjectivity of $M$ on $\operatorname{ran}P$. rows.plain: Correcting a periodic approximate flow on all time intervals
rows.annotation: The endpoint condition in `SeqPerturbation` follows by evaluating the corrected mild formula at zero of each piece: the mixed and quadratic integrals and the local residual vanish there. Multiplying by $\theta^n$ and adding the matching reference gives the required matching of corrected fields.
